quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'very' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The lecture was very informative.
quests.hint: This word strengthens the adjective right after it - keep them together.
quests.explanation: 'Very' intensifies the adjective 'informative', so it sits directly before it: 'very informative'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'very' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She spoke very slowly during the announcement.
quests.hint: This time the word strengthens an adverb instead of an adjective - the rule stays the same.
quests.explanation: 'Very' can also intensify another adverb, sitting directly before it: 'very slowly'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'very' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: This is a very unusual request for our department.
quests.hint: Find the adjective describing the noun, and place the intensifier directly before it.
quests.explanation: 'Very' sits directly before the adjective 'unusual', strengthening the description of the request.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'too' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The soup was too spicy for the children.
quests.hint: This word signals more than acceptable - place it directly before the adjective it affects.
quests.explanation: 'Too' shows the spiciness went beyond what was suitable, so it sits directly before 'spicy': 'too spicy'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'too' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He arrived too late to catch the train.
quests.hint: This word works the same way with an adverb - place it right before 'late'.
quests.explanation: 'Too' sits directly before 'late', showing the lateness caused him to miss the train.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'too' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: This box is too heavy to carry alone.
quests.hint: Apply the same excessive-degree pattern here.
quests.explanation: 'Too' sits directly before 'heavy', showing the weight exceeds what one person can manage.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'quite' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The hotel room was quite small for the price.
quests.hint: With an everyday adjective like this one, this word softens the description slightly - meaning 'fairly'.
quests.explanation: Before a gradable adjective like 'small', 'quite' means 'fairly' and sits directly before it: 'quite small'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'quite' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The results were quite extraordinary.
quests.hint: This adjective already describes something at its extreme - here the same word means 'completely', not 'fairly'.
quests.explanation: Before a strong adjective like 'extraordinary', 'quite' shifts meaning to 'completely', while still sitting directly before it: 'quite extraordinary'.
quests.grammarRule: Degree Adverb Placement - 'Quite' (Gradable vs Non-Gradable Meaning)

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'quite' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The children were quite tired after the hike.
quests.hint: This adjective is an everyday, gradable one, so the softer meaning applies again here.
quests.explanation: Before the gradable adjective 'tired', 'quite' returns to meaning 'fairly', sitting directly before it: 'quite tired'.
quests.grammarRule: Degree Adverb Placement - 'Quite' (Gradable vs Non-Gradable Meaning)

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'rather' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The exam was rather difficult compared to last year's.
quests.hint: This word sits directly before the adjective it modifies, similar to 'quite'.
quests.explanation: 'Rather' sits directly before 'difficult', softening or hedging the claim slightly, a common feature of more formal English.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'rather' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She would rather walk than take the bus.
quests.hint: This is a set preference structure - the word sits right after 'would' and before the verb.
quests.explanation: In the fixed expression 'would rather', the word sits between 'would' and the base verb: 'would rather walk'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'rather' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: It was a rather awkward silence at the dinner table.
quests.hint: Place this word directly before the adjective describing the silence.
quests.explanation: 'Rather' sits directly before 'awkward', softening the description of the silence.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'almost' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Almost everyone at the office signed the card.
quests.hint: This word can attach to a quantity word like 'everyone' - place it directly before that word to show 'not quite all'.
quests.explanation: 'Almost' sits directly before 'everyone', showing that nearly all, but not literally all, of the office signed. Moving it elsewhere would change the meaning entirely.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'nearly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The project is nearly finished after months of work.
quests.hint: This word attaches to the state described by the adjective - place it directly before that word.
quests.explanation: 'Nearly' sits directly before 'finished', showing the project is close to, but not yet at, completion.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'almost' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He almost missed his flight because of traffic.
quests.hint: Unlike the first question, this word now attaches to the action itself - place it directly before the verb.
quests.explanation: Here 'almost' sits directly before the verb 'missed', meaning he came close to missing the flight but caught it - a very different scope from modifying a quantity word like 'everyone'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'barely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She could barely hear the announcement over the noise.
quests.hint: This word sits right after the modal verb, before the main verb, much like 'never' did earlier.
quests.explanation: 'Barely' sits between the modal 'could' and the main verb 'hear', showing the announcement was almost inaudible.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'hardly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: He had hardly started the presentation when the fire alarm rang.
quests.hint: In this perfect structure, place the word between the auxiliary and the past participle.
quests.explanation: 'Hardly' sits between 'had' and 'started', a classic pattern paired with 'when' to show one event interrupting another almost immediately.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'barely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The runner barely finished the marathon before collapsing.
quests.hint: Apply the same modal-free, pre-verb pattern here with a simple past verb.
quests.explanation: 'Barely' sits directly before the main verb 'finished', showing how close the runner came to not finishing at all.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'exactly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: This is exactly what I was looking for.
quests.hint: This word sharpens the precision of the clause that follows - place it directly before that clause.
quests.explanation: 'Exactly' sits directly before 'what I was looking for', sharpening the claim to mean a perfect match.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'exactly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The meeting starts at exactly nine o'clock.
quests.hint: This word pinpoints a precise time - place it directly before the time expression.
quests.explanation: 'Exactly' sits directly before 'nine o'clock', emphasizing there is no room for delay or rounding.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'exactly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: I don't know exactly why the shipment was delayed.
quests.hint: This word can also sharpen a reason clause - place it directly before that clause.
quests.explanation: 'Exactly' sits directly before 'why the shipment was delayed', showing the precise reason is unknown, even if a general reason is known.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'especially' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The staff were especially helpful during the busy holiday season.
quests.hint: This word intensifies the adjective describing the staff - place it directly before that adjective.
quests.explanation: 'Especially' sits directly before 'helpful', singling out this quality as notably strong.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'especially' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: I enjoy reading, especially mystery novels.
quests.hint: This word highlights one specific example from a broader category - place it directly before that example.
quests.explanation: 'Especially' sits directly before 'mystery novels', singling out that specific type of reading from the broader category mentioned first.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'especially' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The traffic gets bad especially during rush hour.
quests.hint: This word can also highlight a specific time - place it directly before that time phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Especially' sits directly before 'during rush hour', singling out that particular time as when the problem is most noticeable.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'almost' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Almost none of the reports were finished on time.
quests.hint: This word sharpens a quantity phrase describing how many reports were affected - place it directly before that phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Almost' sits directly before 'none', showing that a very small number, but not literally zero, were finished on time.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'nearly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Nearly fifty guests attended the wedding reception.
quests.hint: This word softens a specific number - place it directly before that number.
quests.explanation: 'Nearly' sits directly before 'fifty', showing the actual number was close to, but under, fifty.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'hardly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: There is hardly any time left before the deadline.
quests.hint: This word pairs with 'any' to show a very small amount - place it directly before that phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Hardly' sits directly before 'any time', showing that almost no time remains, a common pairing in everyday English.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'especially' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The client seemed especially pleased with the final design.
quests.hint: Recall the pattern from earlier in this file: place the word directly before the adjective it intensifies.
quests.explanation: 'Especially' sits directly before 'pleased', singling out how strong the client's reaction was.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'barely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The budget barely covered the cost of materials.
quests.hint: Recall the pre-verb pattern practiced earlier in this file.
quests.explanation: 'Barely' sits directly before the main verb 'covered', showing the budget was only just enough.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'exactly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The technician wasn't sure exactly when the delivery would arrive.
quests.hint: As before, this word sharpens the precision of the clause that follows it.
quests.explanation: 'Exactly' sits directly before 'when the delivery would arrive', showing the technician knew roughly but not precisely when it would come.
